name: Bush tea for a "washout" or "blood cleanse"
what_people_do: Drink a bitter or purgative bush tea (cerasee and others), often as a regular tonic or at the turn of the year, to "wash out" or "clean the blood".
why_they_say_it_works: The body is said to collect "dirt" or "bad blood" that a bitter tea flushes out; it is also taken to prevent illness.

documented_by.source: Picking D et al 2015, J Ethnopharmacol, PMID 25929450 (TRAMIL survey, Jamaica)
documented_by.quote_or_summary: 407 Jamaican adults named 107 medicinal plants; the survey reports high agreement among informants for "washout and blood cleanse" tonics, nerves and insomnia, and respiratory complaints (as summarised in the agent4 file; abstract confirms 14 plants reached the 20% TRAMIL threshold).

documented_by.source: Clement YN et al 2015, J Ethnobiol Ethnomed, PMID 26369926 (TRAMIL survey, Trinidad)
documented_by.quote_or_summary: 450 rural Trinidad households, 917 single-plant remedies; the 20% "popular use" threshold was met by only a handful of plants (none of them a washout tea in the abstract).

evidence.tested: Laboratory and animal work on three Caribbean plants (cerasee, soursop, anamu)
evidence.population: In vitro and in vivo only
evidence.finding: 13 preclinical studies; no human trial retrieved.

evidence.tested: Whether any bush tea "cleanses the blood"
evidence.finding: My search found no human study of a washout or blood-cleanse effect. "Washout" is not a measurable clinical outcome in the sources I read.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Bitter and purgative teas can cause diarrhoea and dehydration (general pharmacology, not sourced here). A search summary links Jamaican "bush tea" made from Crotalaria to veno-occlusive liver disease (Bras 1954/1957); I did not open the primary papers, so UNVERIFIED.
gaps: No source opened that measures what "washout" means or tests it.
Pyrrolizidine-alkaloid liver risk is UNVERIFIED (primary papers not opened).
Picking 2015 full text not read for tea-by-tea figures.
